topics: Why study in the UK?
Why Manchester Met?
Why your course?
Research process
Career plans
UK connections
Finances
quotes: What other countries did you consider for your studies?
How does the UK education system compare with other countries?
If studying in the UK is more expensive than studying in your home country, why did you decide to make this investment?
What attracted you to Manchester Met?
Did you consider any other universities?
Why did you choose Manchester Met over other universities?
Did you research any university rankings, statistics or student satisfaction data?
Why do you want to study this course?
What are the key modules you'll study?
Which modules are you most interested in, and why?
How is the course taught and assessed?
How did you research your course and university choices?
What sources did you use — websites, rankings, education agents?
What are your career plans once you complete your course?
Do you intend to stay in the UK after your studies, or return home?
Any previous UK visas you've held?
Whether you've ever breached the conditions of a UK visa?
How do you plan to pay for your tuition fees and living costs?
Who is funding your studies, and what's your relationship to them?
Have you researched the cost of living in the UK, particularly in Manchester?
sources.notes: Fetched. Pre-CAS interview is a 'pre-recorded interview' via 'CAS Shield' with a '60-second time limit' per question; 'We may not be able to issue your CAS until we've reviewed your answers.' Also describes the UKVI credibility interview ('usually carried out online, though some are by phone or in person'). Question list is presented as what to prepare for.

sources.title: Apply for your CAS | Manchester Metropolitan University
topics: your course
your finances
your reasons for studying at Manchester Met
overall career plans
sources.notes: Fetched. Verbatim: 'some applicants are asked to complete a short, pre-recorded interview through CAS Shield' and 'there's nothing to prepare beyond answering honestly about your course, your finances, your reasons for studying at Manchester Met and overall career plans'. Separate from any UKVI interview; selected applicants are emailed instructions.

sources.title: Credibility Interviews (Manchester Metropolitan University help sheet PDF, 2 pages)
topics: Why did you choose Manchester Metropolitan University?
Why did you choose your course?
How do your studies fit into your career plans?
What links do you have to the UK?
How will you finance your study?
quotes: Why did you choose Manchester Metropolitan University?
Why did you choose your course?
What is it specifically about this course that you prefer over other course choices?
Did you apply for other courses?
If yes, why did you choose Manchester Metropolitan University over them?
How do your studies fit into your career plans?
How will the knowledge and skills you gain from your programme of study help you with the type of work you hope to do?
Does your course lead to any professional exemptions or qualifications and are these recognised in your home country?
Do you know what others graduating from the course you will be following went on to do?
What links do you have to the UK?
Any previous visas you have had
Whether you have ever breached any of the conditions of your UK Visas
Why you have chosen to return, if you previously studied in the UK
How will you finance your study?
Have you been realistic in assessing the costs of study and how to pay them?
If it is more expensive to pursue your course of study in the UK than in your home country, why have you decided to incur the extra cost?
sources.notes: PDF downloaded by WebFetch and text extracted locally. Help sheet for the Home Office credibility interview: 'There is no guarantee that you will be asked these questions'. Also: 'You could also be asked about any long gaps between your new course and any previous studies. If you are changing course, you may also be asked about the reasons for this.' and 'If the course you plan to study is at a similar academic level to previous studies, be prepared to explain how it represents progression'. 'Manchester Met may ask you to complete an interview with them or your education agent if we feel we need to gather further information from you'.
